newsitem.title: CANADA: Syncrude posts jump in revenue, output on track.
newsitem.headline: Syncrude posts jump in revenue, output on track.

text.p: Syncrude Canada Ltd, the world's largest producer of synthetic crude oil, said on Thursday its third-quarter revenues were 33 percent higher than last year.
Syncrude, which extracts and upgrades bitumen from Alberta's oil sands, also said the operation was on track to produce its 1996 target of 75 million barrels of synthetic crude oil.
The company said revenue for the third quarter increased to C$587 million, up from C$454 million in 1995.
It said the jump was due mostly to higher crude oil prices.

The company said its Syncrude Sweet Blend crude oil averaged C$29.88 a barrel in the period, compared to C$22.65 last year. In September, prices rose to C$31.85 a barrel, their highest since autumn 1990.

Total unit costs for the quarter, including general and administrative, research and financing, fell to C$11.92 a barrel from C$12.24 in the same period last year. Production costs for the quarter declined to C$11.27 a barrel from C$11.41 in 1995.
Output in the period averaged 213,000 barrels a day.

"These results show that Syncrude continues to build upon its outstanding performance in 1995," Syncrude chairman and chief executive Eric Newell said. "The positive impact on revenues and cash flows from higher crude oil prices is reflected in these results."
Newell said the operation's return on capital employed on a 12-month rolling basis was 10.6 percent.

Partners in Syncrude, whose mine and plants are located north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, include Imperial Oil Ltd, Petro-Canada, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, Athabasca Oil Sands Investments Inc, Canadian Oil Sands Investments Inc, Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd unit Mocal Energy Ltd and Murphy Oil Corp.
